newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India picks up after Bombay rise.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India picks up after Bombay rise.

text.p: Indian global depository receipts picked up on Wednesday following gains in Bombay earlier, while Taiwanese issues tentatively extended Tuesday's recovery.
Traders said the third straight gain from local Indian stocks amid good interest had powered GDR gains, but the GDR market itself continued to attract relatively light volumes.
Hindalco added $1.41 to $32.65/33.65 and SBI was 37 cents firmer at $25.00/26.00.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed 1.96 points firmer at 85.43, a 2.35 percent rise, with the premium over the local market at 19.29 percent from 17.91 percent.

The Cazenove Indian GDR index added 2.06 points to 95.53 -- a 18.66 percent premium to the local market from 17.59 percent on Tuesday. It measures from midday on the previous trading day to midday today.
Bombay's benchmark index added 64.84 points to 4,251.13.
Taiwanese GDRs ended mostly better despite late profit-taking in Taipei, and following sharp losses Monday and Tuesday in Taiwanese electronics GDRs.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index added 0.34 points, or 0.26 percent to 131.39, representing a discount to the local market of 2.63 percent from 2.90 percent.
Among key stocks Acer added 10 cents to $15.75/16.50.
Taiwan's weighted index shed 1.77 percent on Wednesday.
The HSBC James Capel Korea GDR Index rose 0.58 points to 74.20 points, a premium of 41.79 percent over the local market.
